data.content_ref: inline:exp-hist:{"target": "a03dc3af0f1149c4accc314193e65e3274a89011c4116bd7dbb4828e265f4189", "seq": 1, "objection": "The target's defense relies on 'verisimilitude' (truth-likeness) to justify preferring better-corroborated theories without induction, but it fails to address the Tichý/Miller proof cited in its own counterconditions. This proof demonstrates that Popper's formal definition of verisimilitude is incoherent for false theories, meaning one cannot logically compare two false theories to determine which is 'closer' to truth. Since the target admits this would overturn its argument if true, and offers no rebuttal to show how the preference remains defensible under this formal collapse, the claim that the preference is 'defensible on Popper's own terms' is unsubstantiated.", "outcome": "raised and not answered; the target's status did not move"}
